q: What is Figure A that is a decorative concrete pavement finished using a patterned template to create surface designs resembling bricks, tiles, or stones?
n: Stenciled concrete is made by laying a paper or plastic stencil on fresh concrete, applying color hardener and lifting the stencil, which leaves grout-line patterns like brick or tile. Source: ACI 310R, Guide to Decorative Concrete.

q: What is Figure B that is a decorative concrete pavement finished by impressing patterns into fresh concrete to give the look of natural materials?
n: Stamped concrete is pressed with rubber texture mats while still plastic, imprinting the look of stone, brick, tile or wood. Source: ACI 310R, Guide to Decorative Concrete.

q: What is Figure C that is a concrete surface with a textured finish created by dragging a tool over it for added slip resistance?
n: A broom finish is made by drawing a stiff broom across freshly floated concrete. The ridges give slip resistance on walks, ramps and driveways. Source: ACI 302.1R; ACI 310R.

q: What is Figure D that is a concrete finish where the top layer is washed off to expose decorative aggregates for a textured look?
n: In a washout (exposed aggregate) finish, a retarder is applied and the surface paste is washed or brushed away, exposing the pebbles for a textured, slip-resistant surface. Source: ACI 310R, Guide to Decorative Concrete.

q: What is Figure E that is a decorative flooring material made from chips of stone or marble set in concrete and polished to a smooth surface?
n: Terrazzo is marble or stone chips set in a cement or epoxy matrix, then ground and polished smooth. Brass or zinc divider strips control cracking. Source: National Terrazzo and Mosaic Association Guide; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What type of tile, shown in Item A, is commonly used in areas exposed to water, such as toilets and swimming pools?
n: Glass mosaic tiles are non-porous, so they absorb almost no water and resist chemicals and stains. That makes them suit pools, showers and toilets. Source: ANSI A137.2 (glass tile); tile manufacturer literature.

q: What material, shown in Item B, is typically used to fill the joints between mosaic tiles for sealing and stability?
n: Grout is a cementitious or epoxy filler pressed into the joints between tiles to seal them, lock the tiles together and keep water out. Adhesive sits underneath the tiles. Source: ANSI A118 (tile installation materials); TCNA Handbook.

q: What type of paving material is Item C, which is fully manufactured and widely used for its durability in paving applications?
n: Concrete pavers are factory-made interlocking units, uniform and very durable, widely used for driveways, plazas and walks. Source: ASTM C936 (solid concrete interlocking paving units); ICPI guidelines.

q: Which type of paving material, shown in Item D, is most suitable for outdoor playgrounds due to its soft, shock- absorbing properties?
n: Rubber pavers, often recycled tires, cushion falls. That is why they are specified for playground surfaces. Source: ASTM F1292 (impact attenuation of playground surfacing).

q: What type of paving material, shown in Item E, is known for being environmentally friendly and often used in sustainable design projects?
n: Natural stone pavers need little manufacturing energy and no binders, last for decades and can be reused, so they suit sustainable design. Source: Natural Stone Institute; LEED materials guidance.

q: What is Figure A, which is commonly used in gardens as stepping stones and floor finishes?
n: Piedra china is a flat river or sea stone, commonly laid as stepping stones and garden paving in Philippine landscaping. Source: Philippine landscape and stone supplier references.

q: What is Figure B, a type of white coral stone commonly used in residential walls?
n: Mactan stone is a white-cream coral limestone quarried in Mactan, Cebu, widely used for house and fence wall cladding. Source: Philippine stone supplier references; Mines and Geosciences Bureau.

q: What is Figure C, which is widely known in Negros and popularly used on both floors and walls?
n: Araal (Aral) slate is quarried in Negros and widely used as floor and wall cladding. Source: Philippine stone supplier references.

q: What is Figure D, which is available in a variety of sizes, shapes, and colors, and commonly used on accent walls?
n: Travertine is a banded limestone available in many cuts, finishes, sizes and colors, popular for accent walls and floors. Source: Natural Stone Institute, Dimension Stone Design Manual.

q: What is Figure E, a building material widely available and made from organic materials?
n: Adobe is sun-dried earth, clay and sand, often mixed with straw or other organic fiber, so the material is widely available and natural. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; ASTM E2392 (earthen wall systems).

q: Which company manufactures local vinyl tiles?
n: Kent is a Philippine-made vinyl floor tile brand. Armstrong is an imported brand, and Diamond and Matimco make other building products. Source: Local building supplier catalogs.

q: Which company is a leading maker of architectural and structural wood products in the Philippines?
n: Matimco Inc. is a leading Philippine maker of treated lumber and engineered wood products for architectural and structural use. Source: Matimco company website.

q: Which of the following is a brand name for acoustic boards?
n: Shera, made by Mahaphant in Thailand, is a fiber cement board brand whose products include perforated acoustic ceiling and wall boards. Source: Shera company website.

q: Which brand of thermosetting plastic laminate is used as a heat- and chemical-resistant surface on furniture and wall panels?
n: Formica is the original brand of high-pressure decorative laminate: thermoset resin and paper layers pressed into a hard, heat- and chemical-resistant surface. Source: Formica Group company website.

q: Which of these is a gypsum board brand?
n: Boral (USG Boral) makes gypsum plasterboard sold in the Philippines. HardieFlex is fiber cement, Mapei is tile adhesives and Matimco is wood products. Source: USG Boral company website.

q: What board covers the bottom of an interior wall to hide the wall–floor joint?
n: A baseboard (skirting) runs along the bottom of a wall to hide the wall–floor joint and protect the wall from knocks and mops. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (interior finishes).

q: What board is placed above curtains to hide the rod and hardware?
n: A curtain cover (curtain box) is a board enclosure above the window that hides the curtain rod and track. Source: Interior design detailing references; Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: What resilient strip on a wall protects it from carts and movable equipment?
n: A wall guard (crash rail or bumper rail) is a resilient or metal strip on walls that takes impacts from carts, beds and trolleys, common in hospitals. Source: DOH Planning and Design Guidelines for Hospitals; manufacturer literature.

q: What piece goes between a door and the floor finish?
n: A threshold (saddle) is set at the door opening between floor finishes. It covers the joint and seals under the door. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (thresholds).

q: What is paneling on the lower part of a wall only called?
n: Wainscoting is paneling or another finish on the lower part of a wall only, typically up to about 0.9–1.2 m, capped with a chair rail. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Which is NOT part of a suspended ceiling framing system?
n: A suspended ceiling frame consists of wall angles, hanger rods or wires, carrying channels and furring channels or tees. Door trim is a door finishing item. Source: ASTM C635/C636 (suspended ceiling systems).

q: What tape is used on gypsum boards before applying plaster or joint compound?
n: Gypsum boards are taped with paper or fiberglass gypsum (drywall/joint) tape, embedded in joint compound so the joint does not crack. Source: Gypsum Association GA-216, Application and Finishing of Gypsum Panel Products.

q: What ceiling hides ductwork while still allowing maintenance access?
n: A suspended (dropped) ceiling hangs below the structure, hiding ducts and pipes in the plenum. Its lift-out panels or access hatches allow maintenance. Source: ASTM C636; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What supports and aligns the panels in a suspended ceiling?
n: Main tee runners hang from the structure and carry the cross tees. Together they form the grid that supports and aligns the lay-in panels. Source: ASTM C635 (suspended ceiling grid).

q: What keeps the joints between gypsum boards from cracking?
n: Joint tape embedded in compound bridges the seam between boards and reinforces it, so movement does not crack the finish. Corner beads protect outside corners. Source: Gypsum Association GA-216.
